section_summary: This section comprises State Department records from 1940 to 1943 concerning Japanese telegraph and cryptographic matters. A major portion documents requests by publishers Pocket Books and Bobbs-Merrill to reissue Herbert O. Yardley's 'The American Black Chamber', which were repeatedly denied by the State, War, and Navy Departments under the Act of June 10, 1933 to safeguard wartime cryptographic operations. The remaining documents include intercepted Japanese diplomatic communications in South America and intelligence from Chungking revealing that Japan broadcast disguised code messages to Buenos Aires via nightly clear Domei news transmissions.

subfiles.about: Records that document 894.727/39 was placed in the confidential file.

subfiles.about: Proposes draft language invoking the 1933 Act against republishing Yardley's book.
subfiles.summary: Suggests language declining permission to republish Yardley's book pursuant to the Act of June 10, 1933.
subfiles.title: Legal Adviser Memorandum on Republication of The American Black Chamber

subfiles.about: Inquires whether the Department objects to a popular-priced edition of Yardley's book.
subfiles.summary: Inquires whether the Department would object to Pocket Books issuing a popular reprint of Yardley's book.

subfiles.about: Informs Pocket Books that reprinting Yardley's book is contrary to the 1933 Act and U.S. interests.
subfiles.summary: Declines permission to republish Yardley's book under the Act of June 10, 1933, citing national interests.
subfiles.title: Letter to Pocket Books Declining Republication Authorization

subfiles.about: Asks how to obtain a copy of the Act of June 10, 1933.
subfiles.summary: Requests a copy of the 1933 Act and notes that obsolete codes should not prevent republication.
subfiles.title: Letter from Pocket Books Requesting Copy of the 1933 Act

subfiles.about: Provides legal citations for the Act of June 10, 1933 in public libraries.
subfiles.summary: Provides citations for the Act of June 10, 1933 in the Statutes at Large and U.S. Code.
subfiles.title: Letter to Pocket Books Providing Statutory Citations

subfiles.about: Requests Department advice on whether reissuing the book conflicts with national security interests.
subfiles.summary: Asks if reissuing the book would contravene public interests, explaining it aimed to alert citizens to subversion.
subfiles.title: Letter from Pocket Books Seeking Policy Advice

subfiles.about: Advises Pocket Books that republishing Yardley's book would not serve national interests.
subfiles.summary: States that after careful consideration the Department believes republishing the book would not serve national interests.
subfiles.title: Letter to Pocket Books Opposing Republication

subfiles.about: Directs immediate recording and routing of incoming correspondence to indicated offices.
subfiles.summary: Routing slip directing the Index Bureau to record and route incoming papers immediately.
subfiles.title: Routing Slip to Index Bureau

subfiles.about: Confirms that Pocket Books will not proceed with publishing Yardley's book.
subfiles.summary: Confirms that Pocket Books will drop plans to publish an edition of Yardley's book.
subfiles.title: Letter from Pocket Books Withdrawing Republication Proposal

subfiles.about: Records file papers checked out from the central filing system.
subfiles.summary: Charge slip recording file papers 894.727/40, /41, and /43 charged to Warren on February 25, 1942.
subfiles.title: Charge Slip for File 894.727

subfiles.about: Transmits a commercial telegram to the Japanese Embassy mistakenly delivered to the American Embassy.
subfiles.summary: Transmits an All America Cables commercial telegram to the Japanese Embassy erroneously delivered to the American Embassy.
subfiles.title: Despatch No. 5097 from Rio de Janeiro Transmitting Japanese Telegram

subfiles.about: Notes an inquiry regarding the admission of Peterson's International Code third edition.
subfiles.summary: Routing slip noting Peterson's International Code third edition reference for William Otterman.
subfiles.title: Office Note on Peterson's International Code

subfiles.about: Reports that Japan will admit Peterson's International Code third edition for messages to major cities.
subfiles.summary: Reports Japan's acceptance of Peterson's International Code third edition on telegrams to Tokyo, Yokohama, Osaka, and Kobe.
subfiles.title: Telegram on Japanese Admission of Peterson's International Code

subfiles.about: Cross-references intercepted Japanese messages decoded at Bandung concerning crisis instructions.
subfiles.summary: Cross-reference file note for Batavia Telegram No. 220 transmitting decoded Japanese diplomatic crisis instructions.
subfiles.title: Cross-Reference File Note for Batavia Telegram No. 220

subfiles.about: Cross-references copies of 50 telegrams to and from the Japanese Legation in La Paz.
subfiles.summary: Cross-reference file note for La Paz Despatch No. 1457 enclosing fifty Japanese code telegrams.

subfiles.about: Transmits lists and details of intercepted telegrams between Tokyo, La Paz, and Lima.
subfiles.summary: Reports that Japanese Foreign Office messages for Lima are decoded via La Paz, transmitting lists of 49 intercepted cables.
subfiles.title: Despatch No. 1459 from La Paz Transmitting Intercepted Japanese Telegrams

subfiles.about: Requests permission under the 1933 Act to republish Yardley's book during the war with Japan.
subfiles.summary: Requests authorization to republish Yardley's book, arguing that public distribution would now serve wartime patriotism.
subfiles.title: Letter from Bobbs-Merrill Requesting Permission to Republish Yardley's Book

subfiles.about: Routes Bobbs-Merrill correspondence to Political Adviser Stanley K. Hornbeck.
subfiles.summary: Routing slip transmitting the Bobbs-Merrill republication inquiry to Political Adviser Stanley K. Hornbeck.

subfiles.about: Retained copy of Bobbs-Merrill's application to republish Yardley's book.
subfiles.summary: Department copy of Bobbs-Merrill's letter requesting authorization to republish The American Black Chamber.
subfiles.title: Copy of Letter from Bobbs-Merrill on Yardley Republication

subfiles.about: Refers Bobbs-Merrill's request to Far Eastern Affairs, finding no patriotic reason to approve it.
subfiles.summary: Refers Chambers's letter to FE, doubting that republication would further the interests of the United States.
subfiles.title: Legal Adviser Memorandum on Bobbs-Merrill Application

subfiles.about: Asks whether the Navy Department has national security objections to republishing Yardley's book.
subfiles.summary: Inquires whether the Navy Department perceives any national security objections to republishing The American Black Chamber.
subfiles.title: Letter to Secretary of the Navy Inquiring on Security Objections

subfiles.about: Asks whether the War Department has national security objections to republishing Yardley's book.
subfiles.summary: Inquires whether the War Department perceives any national security objections to republishing The American Black Chamber.
subfiles.title: Letter to Secretary of War Inquiring on Security Objections

subfiles.about: Directs that attached correspondence be formally entered into Department records.
subfiles.summary: Routing note instructing that the attached correspondence be entered into the central files.
subfiles.title: Department Routing Note for Central Records

subfiles.about: Urges favorable State Department action on Bobbs-Merrill's republication request.
subfiles.summary: Supports constituent publisher Bobbs-Merrill's application to republish Yardley's book and requests advice on its status.

subfiles.about: Informs Representative Ludlow that Bobbs-Merrill's request is receiving careful consideration.
subfiles.summary: Acknowledges Ludlow's letter and states that Bobbs-Merrill's application is receiving careful consideration.
subfiles.title: Letter to Representative Ludlow on Bobbs-Merrill Request

subfiles.about: Summarizes Navy opposition and War Department verbal refusal regarding Yardley's book.
subfiles.summary: Notes Navy's written opposition and Colonel Bratton's telephone confirmation that the War Department opposes republishing Yardley's book.
subfiles.title: Far Eastern Affairs Memorandum on Military Views on Yardley Republication

subfiles.about: Requests an expedited decision on reissuing Yardley's book to meet immediate commercial demands.
subfiles.summary: Thanks Long for an interview and requests a prompt decision regarding reissuance of The American Black Chamber.
subfiles.title: Letter from Bobbs-Merrill Requesting Expedited Action

subfiles.about: Objects to republishing Yardley's book because it would stimulate unwanted curiosity about cryptanalysis.
subfiles.summary: Objects to republishing Yardley's book, warning it would stimulate public curiosity regarding current cryptanalytical operations.
subfiles.title: Letter from Navy Department Opposing Republication

subfiles.about: Informs Bobbs-Merrill that national defense agencies unanimously oppose republication of Yardley's book.
subfiles.summary: Informs Bobbs-Merrill that government agencies unanimously concluded republication of Yardley's book is contrary to national interests.
subfiles.title: Letter to Bobbs-Merrill Denying Republication Permission

subfiles.about: Transmits a copy of the Department's denial letter to Bobbs-Merrill for Ludlow's information.
subfiles.summary: Encloses a copy of the Department's refusal letter sent to the Bobbs-Merrill Company.
subfiles.title: Letter to Representative Ludlow Transmitting Denial Notice

subfiles.about: Transmits a copy of the Department's denial letter to Bobbs-Merrill for Bloom's information.
subfiles.summary: Encloses a copy of the Department's refusal letter to Bobbs-Merrill for Representative Sol Bloom's information.
subfiles.title: Letter to Representative Bloom Transmitting Denial Notice

subfiles.about: Objects to republishing Yardley's book because disclosing War Department methods would aid enemy agents.
subfiles.summary: Opposes republishing Yardley's book because revealing War Department methods would make information accessible to enemy agents.
subfiles.title: Letter from War Department Opposing Republication

subfiles.about: Confirms receipt and messenger delivery of War Department communications.
subfiles.summary: Messenger receipt acknowledging delivery of the War Department's letter concerning the Bobbs-Merrill Company.
subfiles.title: War Department Delivery Receipt

subfiles.about: Records the withdrawal of restricted document 894.727/54 from public access.
subfiles.summary: Notice recording the withdrawal of restricted document 894.727/54, a 1942 letter from Hoover to Berle.
subfiles.title: Withdrawal Notice for Document 894.727/54

subfiles.about: Accepts without question the Government's decision prohibiting republication of Yardley's book.
subfiles.summary: Accepts in good part the Government's decision denying permission to republish The American Black Chamber.
subfiles.title: Letter from Bobbs-Merrill Accepting Adverse Decision

subfiles.about: Cross-references a naval intelligence report transmitting coded Japanese despatches from Bogotá.
subfiles.summary: Cross-reference file note for Report No. 218 transmitting coded Japanese diplomatic despatches sent from Bogotá.
subfiles.title: Cross-Reference File Note for Colombia Naval Attaché Report No. 218

subfiles.about: Records the withdrawal of restricted document 894.727/57 from public access.
subfiles.summary: Notice recording the withdrawal of restricted document 894.727/57, a 1942 letter from Hoover to Berle.
subfiles.title: Withdrawal Notice for Document 894.727/57

subfiles.about: Reports an offer of Japanese intercepts by a Korean contact and relays intelligence on radio ciphers and Soviet relations.
subfiles.summary: Reports a Korean contact's offer of Japanese intercepts from Chinese intelligence, who discounted Yardley's skills. Details intelligence that Japan transmits coded messages via nightly clear Domei broadcasts to Argentina, discusses Russo-Japanese tensions, and notes Japanese assessments following U.S. occupation of Attu Island.
subfiles.title: Telegram No. 1021 from Chungking on Japanese Cryptography and Diplomatic Intelligence

subfiles.about: Official State Department paraphrase of Chungking Telegram No. 1021 for military and naval intelligence.
subfiles.summary: Confidential paraphrase of Telegram No. 1021 detailing Korean intelligence offers, Chinese cryptanalysis, Domei broadcast ciphers, and Russo-Japanese diplomacy.
subfiles.title: Paraphrase of Chungking Telegram No. 1021
subfiles.to: Military Intelligence Division and Office of Naval Intelligence

subfiles.about: Records agreement to request FCC monitoring of nightly Japanese Domei broadcasts to Buenos Aires.
subfiles.summary: Records decision to ask the FCC to monitor nightly Japanese Domei news broadcasts suspected of containing disguised code.
subfiles.title: Memorandum on Monitoring Japanese Domei Radio Broadcasts

subfiles.about: Requests that the FCC monitor nightly Japanese Domei radio broadcasts transmitted to Buenos Aires.
subfiles.summary: Requests that the FCC monitor nightly Japanese Domei newscasts sent to Buenos Aires suspected of concealing code messages.
subfiles.title: Letter to FCC Requesting Monitoring of Domei Broadcasts
